quoted_phrases: These fungi are not decoration on tree roots.
For a tree, this is not a minor upgrade.
Trees do not simply hand over sugar to any fungus in the neighbourhood.
A common mycorrhizal network is not just “fungi in the soil”.

A 2023 review in Nature Ecology & Evolution argued that several strong public claims about common mycorrhizal networks in forests, including that they are widespread, that they reliably improve seedling performance, and that mature trees preferentially send resources to offspring, are not yet supported by enough field evidence.
That does not make the networks imaginary.
The experiment became famous because it suggested that forest plants were not merely competing as isolated individuals.
But a detected transfer is not the same as proof that a mature tree is deliberately feeding a seedling, or that the transfer meaningfully changes survival in all forests.
Forest life is not a morality play about generosity.
But this is not conversation in the human sense.
But mycorrhizal fungi do not simply “store carbon” in a straightforward way.
Seedlings do not enter a neutral underground world.
This is one reason forest recovery is not just a matter of planting stems in the ground.
That does not mean protecting fungi is a simple climate solution.
They are not magical forest internet cables through which wise old trees send care packages to their children.
A forest is not just a collection of trees.
